name: Net migration, ages 10 to 19 in 2020, 2010-2020 (estimate, % of expected)
plain: How many people aged 10 to 19 in 2020 each municipio gained or lost to migration since 2010, per 100 it would have had with no migration.
definition: Net migration between the 2010 and 2020 censuses of the people aged 10 to 19 in 2020 (aged 0 to 9 in 2010), per 100 of the people of that age the municipio would have had with no migration: positive, more came than left; negative, more left. An estimate by the residual method: the 2020 census count of each age group minus the survivors of the same people in the 2010 census, by sex, with Puerto Rico's life table (UN World Population Prospects 2024, 2010-2019). It counts moves to and from the rest of Puerto Rico and abroad together, net; errors in either census land in it, and in small municipios a few hundred people can move the figure.

coverage.frequency: The window 2010-2020, census to census; the next window needs the 2030 census.

method: netmig_age.py compares, for each municipio, sex and five-year age group, the people aged a to a+4 in the 2010 census with the same generation, aged a+10 to a+14, in the 2020 census. Puerto Rico's life table (UN World Population Prospects 2024, the person-years lived by age and sex averaged over 2010-2019) says how many of them would still be alive; the 2020 count minus those survivors is the net migration of the group. Children under 10 in 2020, born during the decade, are left out.
source_detail: Estimated by the observatory: the 2010 and 2020 census counts by municipio, age and sex (Census Bureau estimates files, census bases) and Puerto Rico's life table (UN WPP 2024), by the residual method (netmig_age.py)
how_to_read: Puerto Rico: -17.6%. Lowest: Guánica (-35.4%), Arroyo (-29.8%), Yabucoa (-29.3%). Highest: Isabela (-6.3%), Camuy (-7.0%), Rincón (-7.1%).
caveats: Net: people who moved within Puerto Rico and people who left for or came from abroad are counted together, and arrivals cancel departures.
Errors in either census land in the estimate, and the 2020 census added noise to protect privacy: in small municipios a few hundred people move a rate by several points.
One life table for the whole island: a municipio where people die younger than average shows a little more out-migration than it had.
